traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-two op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as

  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the

  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is

`ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted
  zero-duration activity and inactive display/menu titles (E2-27).
  `TextProps.swift` is the text group and `RecipeReveal` (with format version
  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it
  decodes silently to that key's default (the amount to 1, the rest to nil).
  `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift` mirrors
  `model_graphic.rs`'s `GraphicProps` as `GraphicSnapshot` (`in` is
  `sourceIn`) and `GraphicPropValue` (string, number, bool; anything else
  `.null`), decoded into `ClipSnapshot.graphic`; `props` keys keep the
  module's own spelling (snake-case conversion does not reach a dictionary's
  keys). `WordProps.swift` mirrors `model_words.rs`
  (`TextCase`, `TextWord`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill`, `WordStyle`)
  — `WordStyle.dictionary` writes ALL eight keys (`active_fill` and `pause_dim` since format version 12; `ActivePill.dictionary` writes `glide`), `NSNull` for a nil slot,
  `MotionProps.dictionary`'s rule, because the core deep-merges
  `word_style` — and holds
  what the renderer and the inspector share: `laidContent` (`case` applied —
  every layout and string index is in ITS UTF-16 space, never `content`'s),
  `tokenCount`, `isUntimedPage`, `TextPatch.contentEdit` and
  `InspectorBinding.contentOps` / `ops(textContent:)` — the Content write,
  decided PER CLIP: `words: []` beside the content in one `set_text` only for
  base clips whose count changed, and never `words` in an action end (W-2,
  W-6). It lives there, not in `InspectorPane.swift`, for the size rule.

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`)
  — NSDocument, `.framejob` package read/write, and the single mutation
  point (see Undo); `applyEdit`'s `.refused` arm beeps and then posts
  `projectDocumentDidRefuse` with the `ReelRefusal` (spec §11 CI-10), which
  the editor forwards to the inspector's refusal strip. Holds the SIX pieces of view state nothing persists —
  playhead, clip selection, in/out range, `selectedMedia`, `nestPath` and
  `selectedAction` — re-clamped by `clampViewState` in that order with the
  scope FIRST, since the selection clamp measures against whatever
  container the scope left. `selectedAction` (spec §11 CI-1) is nil or one
  action of the SINGLE selected clip; `+SelectedAction` holds its queries,
  its one deliberate writer `selectAction(_:)` (which stores nil for an id
  that is not `singleSelectedClip`'s) and the ENTRY rule
  `syncSelectedAction()`, run from `playhead`'s and `selection`'s `didSet`
  against `lastInsideAction`. The clamp re-reads `lastInsideAction` BEFORE
  its last line writes the playhead, so an edit, undo or redo under a
  stationary playhead never enters a span — keep those two lines above
  that write. `nestPath` is a
  PATH of (nest, clip) steps, not a nest id, because two clips can show one
  nest at two starts; `editedProject` is a STORED, memoised `rc_project_scoped`
  handle, and `project` still means the parent for save, export and
  consolidate. A range is cleared on every scope change: a pair of ticks means
  one thing inside a nest and another to an export. `+UndoGroup`:
  `inUndoGroupIfRegistered` runs a body with an undo group pending, and
  `registerUndo(restoring:actionName:)`'s first statement
  (`openPendingUndoGroup()`) opens it at the body's first registration, at the
  body's level and never while undoing or redoing; a body that registers
  nothing leaves undo and redo untouched (#167); `registerUndo` stays the one
  registrar. `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)` (#272) undoes the step that ended at
  `step` before committing, when `project` is still that handle, so a strip's
  off-knob double-click is one step. `cacheDirectory` calls `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` when it
  creates `cache/` — only if the package's date, read through a fresh `URL`
  before the create, is still `fileModificationDate`, so an outside change made before it is not absorbed — and that method re-reads the date through a fresh
  `URL`, because `fileURL` still holds the date it cached at open (#138).
  `+CacheSaves` is the `save(to:ofType:for:completionHandler:)` override
  every save funnels through, bracketing it with the cache ledger's
  `saveBegan` / `saveEnded` (#115, #169).
  `+Import` is File ▸ Add Media… and every drop into an open project
  (`importMedia`, the probe chain and the one grouped commit), the opening
  read's probe (`probeForOpening`, a cancelled copy as `.userCancelled`), and the Media
  tab's Relink… and the missing-media sheet's body (`relinkMedia(_:)`: each
  file probed through `MediaImporter.probe`, one grouped "Relink Media" edit
  carrying each descriptor as `relink_media`'s `probe`, spec §11 #63, then
  `generateCaches()`; the missing-media sheet's door then alerts each
  unreadable file and each refused sentence (#180) through `present(_:)`).
  `+MissingCopies` re-copies, on open, a WebM/MKV copy that is missing or in
  the Trash from its recorded original (spec §11 #228-O), through
  `MediaImporter.probeBuiltInCopy` (never ffmpeg, never a question); a
  read on main or inside `withoutAsking` (an agent's `open_project`, off
  main since #231) passes no watch.
  `+Alerts` is `present(_:)`: every error the document shows waits in one
  queue (`DocumentAlertQueue`) and shows one alert sheet at a time, each asked
  for a main-queue turn after the last one's `didPresent` or the window's last
  sheet end, and only while no sheet is attached, since AppKit drops an error
  sheet asked for while another is attached (#195, `relink_sheet_probe.py`
  A1–A5); with no window, it is app-modal at once. `+Graphics`
  is the document's side of the package's `graphics/`:
  `startGraphicStore()`, run from `makeWindowControllers()` and seeding an
  untitled document's root from `autosavedContentsFileURL/graphics`, and
  `graphicsWrapper()`, the lazy wrapper the save whitelist carries — for a
  SAVED document it reads `<fileURL>/graphics` itself and never asks the
  store, so a nil store can never drop a saved folder; for an untitled one
  it carries the store's root only when `GraphicStore.holdsContent` (an
  entry, file or directory, that is neither hidden nor the manual) says so
  (spec §11 G-14).
  `startGraphicStore()` also installs the document's compiled set in
  `GraphicRegistry` and observes the store's `.graphicsDidChange`, whose
  handler updates the registry and THEN posts `.projectGraphicsDidChange`
  (object: the document) — never `rescan()` there; `stopGraphicStore()`, from
  `close()`, removes the observer, drops the set, stops the store and removes
  BOTH untitled roots — the graphics root (`removeScratchRoot()`) and
  `temporaryCacheDirectory` (`removeTemporaryCacheDirectory()`); the cache
  root goes at close ONLY, never at the first save, because the timeline and
  any pass in flight still hold its path (G-19 (d)). `startGraphicStore()` also observes the document's own
  `.projectDocumentDidChange` and ends with one `reconcileGraphicNames()`;
  `stopGraphicStore()` removes that observer. `+ConvertedThumbnails`:
  `startCaches()`, from `makeWindowControllers()` in place of
  `generateCaches()`, observes the document's own `.projectDocumentDidChange`
  and starts a cache pass for each media whose converting Camera Log differs
  from the ledger's `lastInput` (spec §11 GR-21); `stopGraphicStore()` removes
  that observation with the rename repair's. `+GraphicFiles` holds the three
  bodies BOTH doors call — `deleteGraphic(named:)` (refused while a clip
  draws the module, naming the clips per container),
  `renameGraphic(named:to:apply:)` (the file, its history, then one
  `set_graphic {name}` per container handed to `apply` as ONE step, moved
  back when `apply` throws or leaves a clip behind, the journal put back as
  it was read before the rename — only when the move back succeeded, so a
  failed one keeps its pair for the repair (G-28 (d)); refused with a nest
  open) and `restoreGraphic(named:revision:)` (which refuses a kept file
  whose bytes are not the revision in its name, G-29 (d)) — each ending its
  file act in one `rescan()`, every throw of its own a `ReelCoreError`; and
  the repair `reconcileGraphicNames()` (spec §11 G-28 (e)): after every
  committed change and once at the store's start, a journalled pair `[a, b]`
  says the app moved the file from `a` to `b`, and when a clip draws `a`,
  with no file and NO kept revision, while `b` has a file and no clip, the
  file is moved back from `b` — one direction only, never from a pair's
  first name to its second (G-28 (e), (f)) — and a file-less name WITH kept
  revisions is left alone even when a crash inside a rename, not a delete,
  left it so (G-28 (f)): it is otherwise a deleted module (G-27 (f)). Never
  call it, or any of the three bodies, from a `.graphicsDidChange` or
  `.projectGraphicsDidChange` observer.
- `MediaImporter.swift` (+`Probe`, +`Speech`, +`Peaks`, +`Color`: the
  Apple Log and Apple Log 2 labels read at probe, spec §11 GR-16, and
  `detectedPQ`, a PQ file's HDR10 peak through `ReelHDR10`, HD-6, and
  `detectedStillPQ`, a PQ still's through `ReelHDR10.stillPeak`, HD-20;
  +`ThumbnailSource`: the converted strip, below; +`Thumbnails`: the
  await-free halves of `thumbnails`, the image branch and the publish) ·
  `MediaPeakBuckets.swift` · `MediaCacheFiles.swift` · `MediaCacheLedger.swift` ·
  `MediaCacheLane.swift` ·
  `FFmpegRewrap.swift` (+`Plan`) · `AppSupport.swift` · `DecoderSupport.swift` ·
  `CodecLibraries.swift` (the SVT-AV1 and libvpx link and its `-RCCodecProbe`;
  export rows arrive with road map codec-export's C1) ·
  `ContainerRewrap.swift` (+`Writer`) · `RewrapProgress.swift` ·
  `RewrapProgressWindowController.swift` — the import funnel and the three per-media caches (`thumbs/`, `peaks/`,
  `speech/`) inside the package. `DecoderSupport.swift` (await-free) is the
  per-process opt-in to macOS's supplemental VP9 and AV1 decoders (`enable()`:
  `main.swift`, `generateCaches`, `CompositionBuilder.firstTrack`, the harness
  and the formats probe), the import's one-frame decode (`decodesFirstFrame`,
  refusing only for `refusingErrorCodes`, -11833 and -11855) and the codec
  refusal sentence (`refusal`), spec §11 #216. `ContainerRewrap.swift`
  (+`ContainerRewrapWriter.swift`, both await-free) opens a WebM or Matroska
  file with no question (spec §11 #216-R): the core indexes it through
  `ReelContainer`, the first video and audio streams are copied unchanged by
  `AVAssetWriter` into `Rewrapped/` under `FFmpegRewrap.destination(for:)`'s
  digest name, the movie's timescale the least common multiple of 600 and
  the tracks' timescales (`ContainerRewrapWriter.movieTimeScale`, spec §11
  #232), an SDR copy labelled from its Colour element or else a VP9 keyframe's
  `stream_matrix` (`ContainerRewrapWriter.sdrLabels`, spec §11 CX-16 (10)), the free space is checked first, #216's codecs are refused
  before the copy, and a codec the copy does not carry (`.unsupported`) alone
  falls through to the opt-in ffmpeg step. `RewrapProgress.swift` +
  `RewrapProgressWindowController.swift`: a click door's copy reports to a
  non-modal window shown after 1 s, which never takes the keyboard from a
  Frame Job window, and Cancel removes the partial copy (spec §11 #228-P). A
  tool call passes no watch.
  `MediaCacheLane.swift` (await-free) is `MediaImporter.CacheLane`, the cache
  lane: every pass's peaks, sync and speech decodes run on it, at most two at
  a time, first in first out, on a queue of its own and never on the Swift
  cooperative pool, where synchronous reads would stop every `AVAssetReader`

`AppSupport.ensureDirectory` is the ONE creator of that folder and of any
  folder under it: `0700` at each level it makes, an existing folder left
  alone (#108).
- `MediaConsolidator.swift` (+`EditorViewController+Consolidate`) — writes
  inside the package behind NSDocument's back, so it MUST call
  `ProjectDocument.packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` afterwards.
- `GraphicStore.swift` — one document's `graphics/` (road map 10 §5f):
  where it is (`<package>/graphics`, or an untitled document's
  `<NSTemporaryDirectory()>/FrameJob/<UUID>-graphics`, re-pointed by
  `packageDidMove(to:)` from the `fileURL` setter, posting
  `.graphicsLocationDidChange`), the scan (each legal `*.js` with its
  SHA-256 revision, G-13; `fonts/` validated on a throwaway
  `GraphicLibrary` once per file identity — size, modification date and
  file number — in `GraphicStore+Fonts.swift`'s `validatedFonts`, whose
  `fontVerdicts` is queue-confined and survives `stop()`/`start()` (spec
  §11 G-23 (f)); `assets/` with a 0-byte file, or a name `asset(name)`
  cannot use, warned and skipped, G-23 (e)) and the watch. **`graphics/` is created on the app's first write, never at
  open** (G-14): `ensureFolder()` is the ONE creator inside a package, and
  every app-side writer goes through `write(name:source:)` or it. While the
  folder is absent the store watches the PACKAGE directory, and the first
  observed appearance calls `folderDidAppear` →
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` once — without it the next save is
  refused as "changed by another application". A folder source raises
  `.write` only and an in-place save raises nothing on it (G0 q7), so each
  module, font and asset file has its own source, up to `fileSourceLimit` (16
  a pass, modules first, then fonts, then assets, each in name order; spec §11
  G-19 (c), G-20 (a)); a source whose `open` fails is a scan warning,
  "`<subject>` is not watched: open failed (`<strerror>`)", `errno` copied
  first (G-20 (b); `GraphicScan.warnings`, shown by the Source section and `get_graphic {}`,
  G-24 (b));
  every pass re-opens every source BY PATH and
  arms BEFORE it scans; events coalesce over 100 ms. The queue owns the diff
  and an outbox; main publishes in order through `drain()` (`scan`, the
  callback, `.graphicsDidChange` with sorted names — every module and
  `library: true` when the font/asset set moved; with NO names when the
  folder holds no module and only the library moved, which still posts, G5b).
  `GraphicStore+Files.swift` holds the store's own writes:
  `uniqueModuleName(_:)`, the one free-name rule (`-copy`, `-copy-N`)
  Duplicate and Insert ▸ Graphic share, which takes a name as held when the
  scan OR the disk has it (`holdsModule(named:)`, #75); `write(name:source:)`
  and `importFile` land through `land(at:writing:)`, whose `.partial` is
  removed on any failure; and `removeScratchRoot()`, which removes an untitled
  root after `stop()` — from `packageDidMove(to:)` and `stopGraphicStore()`
  (G-19 (d)). It also holds the app's delete and rename, each inside
  `onQueue` (main only, never on the store's queue) so no pass runs between
  their steps: `removeModule(named:)` keeps the file's bytes and then removes
  it, refusing when the text could not be kept, and `moveModule(from:to:)`
  moves the file, journals the pair and reads it back — a rename that cannot
  be journalled is refused — and then moves its history, a throw leaving the
  file and the history where they were and the journal put back as it was
  read (its bytes, or no file: `renameJournalBytes` / `putBackRenameJournal`
  in `GraphicStore+History.swift`), so a refused rename journals no pair; a
  crash between the three steps is G-28 (f)'s limit; neither rescans.
  `write(name:bytes:)` is `write(name:source:)` for bytes as they are, and
  `noModuleSentence(_:)` the one sentence for an absent module.
  `GraphicStore+History.swift` is the kept revisions and the rename journal
  (spec §11 G-27..G-29): `graphics/history/<name>/<%06d sequence>-<revision>.js`,
  the last `historyLimit` (10) per module, and `history/renames.json`, at
  most `renameJournalLimit` (32) pairs. `keepReplaced`, called by `pass` on
  the queue before it stores its scan, keeps the bytes a module's new text
  replaced and drops the new text's own revision, so history never holds the
  current text; nothing is kept at `start()` or for a removal the app did not
  make, and `start()` drops each module's current revision from its history.
  `history/` is created only inside an existing `graphics/` (G-14) with no
  `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` call, and `moveHistory` leaves no
  `history/<from>/` behind — which is what makes 'no file, something kept'
  mean a DELETED module. `GraphicStore+Import.swift`'s `importAsset` files a name
  `asset(name)` cannot use under `GraphicAssetName.legalized`, a renamed
  copy taking `-2`, `-3`, … while `holdsAsset(named:)` (scan or disk) says
  the name is held, and answers `name`/`renamedFrom` (G-23 (c), (d)). **`drain()` is not
  re-entrant: never call `rescan()` from a `.graphicsDidChange` observer.**
  `stop()` bumps a generation under `queue.sync`. `makeLibrary()` is a NEW
  builder every call (a library freezes on first use). It also writes the
  app's bundled reference into an EXISTING folder as `API.md` and `API.d.ts`
  (`writeManual()`, from `start()` for a saved package, `ensureFolder()` and
  `write()`; only when the bytes differ) — never a reason to create the
  folder (G-14).
- `GraphicScan.swift` — `GraphicModuleFile`, `GraphicFile` and `GraphicScan`,
  what one pass of the store found. `GraphicAssetName.swift` — pure: G-23's
  asset-name rule (`isLegal`, `legalized`, `withSuffix`, `maxBytes` 247 —
  255 less `.partial` — `rule`, `renameNotice`). `GraphicStore+Fonts.swift`
  — `GraphicFontIdentity`, `GraphicFontVerdict` and the scan's font pass,
  `validatedFonts(_:)`, queue only. `GraphicTemplates.swift` — pure: the
  bundled `GraphicTemplates/` modules (copied by `project.yml`'s post-build
  script), their titles from the file stem (never compiled — every chrome
  probe builds the menu bar) and a stem sanitised to a legal module name.
  `GraphicStore+Manual.swift` — the
  manual: `manualNames` (`API.md`, `API.d.ts`), `bundledManualNames`
  (`GraphicsAPI.md`, `GraphicsAPI.d.ts`, copied into Resources by
  `project.yml`'s post-build step from `docs/`), `manualDirectory(besideFonts:)`,
  `writeManual()` and `holdsContent`.
  [] and the map is kept. `TimelineView+SourceMap.swift` is
  the filmstrip's and the waveform's map-aware `sourceTime`
  (`TimelineView.swift` is frozen; it holds only `sourceMaps`, set in
  `refreshTimeline` from the same handle as the snapshot).

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**The editor.**
- `EditorViewController+Graphics` refreshes the paused frame on
  `.projectGraphicsDidChange` for its own document.
  appends the plan too.
- `+AddClips` (Add Text / Add Shape: the front track, else a new one;

  when the edit lands outside the menu's event, as a panel's completion does),
  `+GraphicMenus` (Insert ▸ Graphic's templates and From File…, File ▸ Add
  Font/Image to Graphics…; the template item runs in-event through
  `applyEdit`, the panels through `performGroupedEdit`; the shared body
  `insertGraphic(from:grouped:) throws` shows no dialog, and a module that
  does not compile stays on disk and places nothing — G-16; a file that is not
  UTF-8 is refused by name before anything is written (#75); Add Image to
  Graphics…'s body is `addGraphicImage(from:) throws` (no panel), which
  shows `showGraphicNotice`'s informational sheet when the picture was
  renamed, G-23 (d); its `validateGraphicMenuAction` answers the four and
  forwards every other action to `validateGraphicFileAction`),
  `+GraphicFiles` (File ▸ Rename Graphic…, Delete Graphic… and Restore
  Graphic Version…, spec §11 G-30: three `@objc` actions, the ONE
  `presentAsSheet` of `GraphicFileSheetController`, in
  `presentGraphicFileSheet`, which beeps when the item has nothing to
  offer, and the validator arm `validateGraphicFileAction` — something to
  list, and for Rename no nest open; Rename and Restore open on the ONE
  selected clip's graphic when it is a row, a deleted one included, and
  Delete always on the first; nothing there writes a file or applies an
  op),
  `+Clipboard` (⌘X/⌘C/⌘V over the `com.kgalligan.framejob.clips` pasteboard,
  the `paste` op's payload; ⌥⌘V Paste Attributes with no `groups`; and
  Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties, whose `@objc` action
  the outlines stay drawn under them.
- `EditorWindowController.swift`, `WelcomeWindowController.swift`,
  `AppDelegate.swift` (+`Menus`, +`ClipMenus` — the Clip menu's submenus, Add
  Background, Transition, Motion, Look and Label, a pure move out of `+Menus`,
  grading GR1 — +`Recording`, +`Updates` — Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…
  and the Sparkle updater, compiled only under `FRAMEJOB_UPDATER`
  (Distribution, spec §11 PUB-6..PUB-9) —, +`GraphicMenu` — the Insert
  menu's builder (Adjustment Clip first, then Graphic ▸), File's three graphic-file items (`addGraphicFileItems(to:)`,
  called once from `fileMenu()` right after Add Image to Graphics…: a
  separator, then Rename Graphic…, Delete Graphic… and Restore Graphic
  Version…, no key equivalents, spec §11 G-30) and Help ▸ Graphics
  Reference, `showGraphicsReference`, on the delegate), `main.swift` — the window,
  the no-document window, the launch/terminate flow and the whole menu bar
  (spec §9). Menu items are nil-target selectors down the responder chain.
  `AppDelegate.swift` binds the agent socket at launch, then calls
  `ProjectDocumentController.complainUnlessShared()`, and releases the

  its composition was built (an export or `render_frame` key falls back to its

  module, font and asset file has its own source, up to `fileSourceLimit` (16

// lower-third — road map 10 §5k 1: a slide-in bar and title on a spring, a
// staggered subtitle, and an outro keyed to durationInFrames.
export const meta = {
  name: "Lower third",
  durationInFrames: 150,
};

export const schema = {
  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const u = ctx.height / 1080;
  const size = props.size * u;
  const sub = size * 0.5;
  const titleFont = { family: "Montserrat", size, weight: 800 };
  const subFont = { family: "Montserrat", size: sub, weight: 800 };
  const titleWidth = measureText(props.title, titleFont).width;
  const subWidth = measureText(props.subtitle, subFont).width;
  const boxWidth = Math.max(titleWidth, subWidth) + 80 * u;
  const boxHeight = size + sub + 70 * u;
  const margin = 96 * u;
  const left = props.align === "left" ? margin
    : props.align === "right" ? ctx.width - margin - boxWidth
    : (ctx.width - boxWidth) / 2;
  const top = ctx.height - margin - boxHeight;
  const slide = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-boxWidth - margin, 0], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
  const grow = spring({ frame: frame - 4, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 14 });
  const subIn = spring({ frame: frame - 12, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 16 });
  const out = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0], { clamp: true });
  const x = left + slide;
  const box = props.boxed
    ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${top}" width="${boxWidth * grow}" height="${boxHeight}" fill="#101014" fill-opacity="0.82"/>`
    : "";
  return svg(ctx, `

# graphic/CLAUDE.md — the graphics engine's rules

Applies to everything under `graphic/`, the crate that draws a graphic clip
(road map 10: `designs/adr/roadmap-10-graphics.md`; the full design is
`archive/roadmap-10.md` §5a). Build commands are the root
`CLAUDE.md`'s: `make test` and `make lint` run this crate after the core.
The crate's record is road map 10 §10.4.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, module declarations and re-exports
  only. No implementation code.
- `diagnostic.rs` — `Level`, `Diagnostic` (`{level, message, line, column,
  frame}`, §5b) and its JSON, keys in that order.
- `images.rs` — the decoded-image cache (spec §11 G-39, #127): `Asset
  {data, digest}`, a process-wide `Mutex` map from an asset's own SHA-256
  to `Ready`/`Building`/`Refused`/`Skipped {len}`, `set_image_cache_limit`,
  `image_cache_bytes`, the doc-hidden `image_cache_builds`, `cached_kind`,
  and the builder of a stored-deflate RGBA8 PNG copy, used only when it
  decodes to exactly the original's pixmap and `imagesize` reads the same
  size. No lock is held across a decode, an encode or a usvg call; a
  build writes only while its digest is still `Building`; the default limit
  is 0, so a binary that sets none takes the original route. The doc-hidden
  `set_image_build_hook` installs an `ImageBuildHook` every build calls
  between its two locks with none held, so a test can hold a build there.
- `library.rs` — `Library`: the font set (`fontdb`, from bytes, never
  `load_system_fonts`, G-6) and the asset map (each asset keeps its own
  SHA-256; a PNG or JPEG kind is asked of the cache first), their content `version`
  (SHA-256 with length prefixes), the `measure_text` memo, and the
  crate-private `options()` builder whose resolvers record into a `Probe`
  what resvg never reports. The generic families map to bundled faces
  (`serif` Source Serif 4, `sans-serif` Source Sans 3, `monospace` IBM Plex
  Mono, G-6), and `select_font` queries only the text's own families,
  never usvg's appended serif fallback, so a missing family still draws
  nothing and is warned.
- `raster.rs` — `rasterize`, `MAX_SIDE`, the RGBA→BGRA row copy into the
  caller's strided buffer, and every warning text `rasterize` answers:
  missing family, unparseable `font-family` (the scan of attributes, `style`
  attributes and `<style>` sheets, and the family of a `font` shorthand in
  a `style` attribute or sheet), unknown href, data: URL, non-image
  asset, size mismatch. The texts are load-bearing: tests match them and
  the app shows them on the clip.
- `measure.rs` — `FontStyle`, `TextFont` (with `preserve_space`, the
  `xmlSpace` key, G-22), `TextMetrics`, `measure_text`; a generic family
  is written unquoted.
- `module.rs` — `Module` (`Send + Sync + Clone`, holds no QuickJS object):
  `compile`, the SHA-256 revision (G-13), `meta`/`schema` read through
  `JSON.stringify` in the module's key order (`{}` when not exported),
  `defaults()`, its top-level warnings (`warnings()`, G-21 (b)).
- `runtime.rs` — `Engine` (one QuickJS `Runtime` + `Context` per (thread,
  module), §5b's limits, the interrupt deadline), the `thread_local!` map
  swept by `Weak` before each call, at most `ENGINES_PER_THREAD` (16, spec
  §11 G-21) engines with the least recently used evicted after the call,
  `svg`, `Engine::parse_colours` (the stdlib's `__parseColour` per text
  under one deadline, storing nothing; G-25), `engine_count`, `HEAP_BYTES`,
  `STACK_BYTES`, `SVG_BYTES` (8 MiB, spec §11 G-20 (c)). The crate's one
  clock.
- `sandbox.rs` — the sandbox script (G-5) and the loader that resolves no
  specifier, with `IMPORT_REFUSAL`.
- `exception.rs` — QuickJS error → Diagnostic: `{name}: {message}`, the
  position from `stack` (the module's own frame first), the budget's
  sentences, what `render` returned (a string over `SVG_BYTES` refused by its
  length, before the `<svg` check). The texts are load-bearing.
- `host.rs` — the globals `__measureText`, `__assetNames`, `__warn` and
  `__namedColour` (svgtypes' named-colour table for the stdlib's colour
  parser).
- `props.rs` — `check_schema` (compile, strict; it takes a colour reader,
  which `Module::compile` builds from `Engine::parse_colours` over the
  schema's colour defaults, G-25 (a); a non-boolean `animate` on an entry

`getPointAtLength`, `evolvePath`): pure JavaScript, a curve measured as
  64 chords, a draw-on dashed by the longest subpath, the last paths
  memoised per engine (at most 32, at most 50,000 chords and characters) —
  a cache that changes no answer, held in a closure no module can reach.
  No helper answers `Infinity` or NaN: a path that would make one do so
  is refused in the parse sentence (five checks through one predicate,
  `finite`; `path.test.js`'s row `T8 a number that is not finite`).

## Rules

- **The crate takes bytes and answers bytes** (G-2, G-5): no file system,
  environment or network anywhere in `src/`, and no clock except the call
  deadline. `rg 'std::(fs|env|net)' graphic/src` must print nothing, and
  `rg -n 'std::time' graphic/src` must print exactly one line, the import
  in `src/runtime.rs`: the interrupt deadline stops a call that runs too
  long and feeds no pixel, so a frame stays a function of G-5's inputs.
  Tests may read files and the clock; `src/` may not.
- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` stays in `lib.rs`.
- Every `src/` file stays under 400 lines.
- Tests are black-box in `tests/`, through `graphic::` only, and every claim
  is an oracle — a pixel read back through `common::pixel`, an exact
  message, a comparison of two answers. The one exception is
  `tests/pins.json` (road map 10 §5l), a tripwire for upgrades.
- The root `CLAUDE.md`'s FFI three-file rule does not apply here: no `rc_*`
  export lives in this crate. G1d's `core/src/ffi_graphic.rs` is its one
  caller.
- **No closure handed to usvg holds the probe lock across a usvg call.** A
  nested SVG asset is parsed by `Tree::from_data_nested` inside
  `resolve_string`, and usvg forwards our `select_font` into that parse on
  the same thread; `std::sync::Mutex` is not re-entrant, so a lock held
  across it hangs the render. Each closure calls usvg first and locks only
  for its own push afterwards. `tests/families.rs`'s nested-asset case is
  the oracle.
- `usvg::Options` is not `Clone`: build it per call with `options()`.
- **`Engine`'s fields drop in declaration order: `render`, then the
  context, then the runtime.** Reversing them aborts the process in
  QuickJS's `JS_FreeRuntime`; `tests/module.rs`'s
  `dropped_modules_engines_are_swept` is the oracle (it SIGABRTs). A
  runtime never leaves the thread that made it, and the thread map's
  `RefCell` is never borrowed while JavaScript runs.
- The module is an ES module evaluated UNWRAPPED, so stack positions are
  the file's own. The standard library and the sandbox are scripts, which
  rquickjs names `eval_script`; `position` prefers the module's frame over
  theirs (`render.rs`'s positioned-throw test and the sandbox's
  `math_random` are the oracles).
- `tests/pins.json` is re-pinned with `GRAPHIC_REPIN=1 cargo test
  --release --test pins`, only after looking at the PNGs a mismatch
  writes to `target/pins/`.
- **The modules of `tests/graphics/` are the bundled templates** (Insert ▸
  Graphic; project.yml's "Copy Graphic Templates" lists each). Every one
  except `common::FIXTURES` is held to spec §11 G-44 by
  `tests/templates.rs`: inside title-safe at every frame at 1920×1080,
  1080×1920 and 1080×1080, with defaults, every combination of `enum` options
  and every `string` long (`tests/templates/long_text.rs` must name each), a
  card's background static, the last frame bare, no warning, no `NaN`.

## Dependencies, and why each

- `resvg` 0.48.1, `default-features = false`, features `text`,
  `raster-images`, `svgz`: its defaults minus `system-fonts` and
  `memmap-fonts`, which reach the file system — off for G-6 (the fonts are
  the bundled faces and the package's) and G-2 (the crate reads no files),
  NEVER for size. Binary size and build time are not reasons to leave a
  feature out. `raster-images` is required: without it resvg draws no PNG,
  JPEG, GIF or WebP `<image>`.
- `tiny-skia` 0.12.0 (resvg 0.48.1's pin) is VENDORED and patched in
  `graphic/vendor/` (spec §11 PR-13): a dither stage on every gradient, so a
  gradient does not band at 8 bits. Both `graphic/Cargo.toml` AND
  `core/Cargo.toml` carry the `[patch.crates-io]` table — Cargo ignores a
  dependency's `[patch]`, and the staticlib the app links is built from
  `core/` (`a_gradient_is_dithered_through_the_ffi` guards it). The patch is
  `vendor/tiny-skia-dither.diff`, regenerated by the one command in
  `vendor/README.md` and kept byte-equal to the vendored tree; a resvg
  upgrade that moves tiny-skia re-vendors, re-applies that diff and re-pins
  `tests/pins.json`'s gradient entries.
- `serde_json` with `preserve_order`: JSON key order is part of the
  contract (the Diagnostic's and TextMetrics' keys; a module's schema).
- `sha2`: the Library's content version.
- `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg 0.48.1's own pin): parse `font-family` exactly as
  usvg does, so the scan agrees with usvg on what failed; and its
  named-colour table (`__namedColour`), so a colour name means what usvg
  draws.
- `simplecss` 0.2 (usvg's own pin; usvg does not re-export it): read
  `<style>` sheets and `style` attributes as usvg does.
- `rquickjs` 0.14.0 with `loader` only: quickjs-ng 0.16.2, vendored and
  built by `rquickjs-sys`. `loader` exists for `set_loader`; the resolver
  and loader installed refuse every specifier, and none of rquickjs's own
  loaders (which reach the file system) is used.
- `png` 0.18 (tiny-skia 0.12's own decoder, already in the lock): decode as
  `Pixmap::decode_png` does and write the stored copy (G-39); still the
  pins' PNG dump.
- `zune-jpeg` 0.5 (resvg 0.48.1's own JPEG decoder): decode as resvg does,
  so a JPEG's copy is checked against resvg's own pixels.
- `imagesize` 0.15 (usvg's own size reader): check a copy's size reads the
  same as its original's.
- Dev: `flate2`, to gzip an `.svgz` asset in a test.

content.content:
tool(
                "redo",
                "Redoes one undone step — Edit ▸ Redo (⇧⌘Z). Any new edit clears the redo "
                    + "stack, exactly as in the app.",
                [:]),
        ]
        // The clip and action rows are `AgentCatalog+Clips.swift`'s, spliced in HERE
        // rather than appended, because the catalog's order is the order an agent reads
        // the tools in. The four locals it is handed are the ones a LATER group asks
        // for too — the clip SENTENCE is hoisted here for exactly that reason, since
        // the transition rows below take the property built from it — which is why
        // they stayed on this side of the cut.
        catalog += clipAndActionTools(
            ticks: ticks, trackDescription: trackDescription,
            colorDescription: colorDescription, clipDescription: clipDescription)
        // The two transition rows go HERE, beside `set_transition` and
        // `set_transition_duration` at the end of that group, and never at
        // the end of the catalog — `recording_probe.py` reads the last
        // eleven names, which are the FILE tools.
        catalog += transitionTools(ticks: ticks, clipDescription: clipDescription)
        // The two graphic rows (AgentCatalog+Graphics.swift) follow them, for
        // the same reason: never at the end of the catalog.
        catalog += graphicTools(
            ticks: ticks, trackDescription: trackDescription, clipDescription: clipDescription)
        catalog += [

            // MARK: Tracks

            opTool(
                "add_track",
                "Adds an empty track. INDEX 0 IS THE BACK of the layer stack — the bottom lane "
                    + "of the timeline, drawn first — and tracks.count is the front, which is "
                    + "what ⇧⌘N adds and where an overlay belongs.",
                [
                    "index": "Where in the stack (0 = back). Default: the front.",
                    "name": "Track name, e.g. \"Titles\".",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "remove_track",
                "Removes a track. A track that still holds clips is refused unless with_clips "
                    + "is true, which removes them with it.",
                [
                    "track": trackDescription,
                    "with_clips": "Remove the track's clips too (default false).",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "move_track",
                "Reorders the layer stack: the track moves to `index`, 0 being the back. A "
                    + "higher index draws in FRONT of the tracks below it.",
                ["track": trackDescription, "index": "New position."]),
            opTool(
                "set_track",
                "Renames a track, flips its four switches — the track header's toggles, "
                    + "Track ▸ Hide Video / Mute Audio / Lock Track / Solo — or sets its matte, "
                    + "Track ▸ Matte. hidden drops its "
                    + "picture from the composition, muted its sound; locked keeps every ripple, "
                    + "insert and range edit off it; solo silences every OTHER track in its "
                    + "container (the timeline, or a nest's own tracks) that is not also soloed "
                    + "— mute wins on a track that is both, and pictures are untouched. matte "
                    + "makes the track a matte for the track directly behind it in its "
                    + "container: its clips are not drawn, and what they show cuts that track "
                    + "by alpha, inverted alpha, luma or inverted luma — where the matte track "
                    + "shows nothing, the track behind shows uncut; a back-most matte track, or "
                    + "one in front of another matte track, cuts nothing. Its clips still "
                    + "sound. \"none\" makes it an ordinary track again.",
                [
                    // The four switches name the MENU ITEM each one mirrors
                    // and nothing else: what each DOES is the sentence above,
                    // and a sentence written twice is what this candidate
                    // exists to delete. The description an agent reads comes
                    // with these in one tool object, so nothing is lost.
                    "track": trackDescription,
                    "name": "New track name.",
                    "hidden": "Track ▸ Hide Video.",
                    "muted": "Track ▸ Mute Audio.",
                    "locked": "Track ▸ Lock Track.",
                    "solo": "Track ▸ Solo.",
                    "matte": "Track ▸ Matte; \"none\" is its Off.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "remove_empty_tracks",
                "Removes every track that holds no clips — Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks.",
                [:]),

            // MARK: Markers

            opTool(
                "add_marker",
                "Drops a marker on the timeline. Markers snap to frames and two may not share a "
                    + "time, so a second marker on the same frame is refused. A chapter marker "
                    + "also becomes a chapter in the exported file (M2).",
                [
                    "at": "Where, \(ticks) Default: the playhead.",
                    "name": "Marker name. Default: Marker <n>.",
                    "chapter": "Also a chapter of the exported movie (default false).",
                    "color": "Colour NAME, e.g. \"red\" — not a hex string.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "set_marker",
                "Moves or renames a marker, or changes its colour or chapter flag.",
                [
                    "marker": "Marker id.",
                    "time": "New time, \(ticks)",
                    "name": "New marker name.",
                    "chapter": "Make it a chapter of the exported movie, or stop being one.",
                    "color": "Colour name.",
                ]),
            opTool("remove_marker", "Removes a marker.", ["marker": "Marker id."]),

            // MARK: Canvas

            opTool(
                "set_canvas",
                "Changes the project's canvas — the fixed frame every clip is composited into. "
                    + "rescale_clips multiplies every clip's x, y and scale by the size ratio, "
                    + "which is what keeps a layout looking the same when you resize; without "
                    + "it the clips keep their pixel positions. Changing fps re-snaps every clip "
                    + "start and duration to the new frame grid.",
                [
                    // The 16–16384 is NOT repeated in either sentence: it is
                    // the core's own bound, published as a minimum and a
                    // maximum from the constants `edit_canvas.rs` refuses by
                    // (`op_table.rs`), and a number spelled twice is what
                    // this whole candidate deletes.
                    "width": "Canvas width in pixels.",
                    "height": "Canvas height in pixels.",
                    "fps": "Frame rate as [numerator, denominator]: [30, 1], "
                        + "[30000, 1001] for 29.97, [24000, 1001] for 23.976.",
                    "background": colorDescription("Colour behind every layer"),
                    "rescale_clips": "Scale every clip's placement with the canvas "
                        + "(default false).",
                    "fit_new_clips": "Give a new clip Fit scale when its source is bigger "
                        + "than the canvas.",
                    "timecode_frames": "Show times as HH:MM:SS:FF rather than HH:MM:SS.mmm.",
                    "output": "The project's dynamic range: \"sdr\" (Rec. 709, the default) or "
                        + "\"hlg\" (HDR, Rec. 2100 HLG). Switching keeps every grade's settings, "
                        + "and a chroma key keeps keying the colour it was picked on; a "
                        + "qualifier's ranges read the HLG signal, so re-pick them after "
                        + "switching. UI: Document tab ▸ Canvas ▸ Dynamic Range.",
                    "blending": "How layers blend: \"encoded\" (the default) or \"linear\" "
                        + "light, where a dissolve keeps its brightness and soft edges and glows "
                        + "come out brighter; grades, keys and qualifiers read what they did. "
                        + "UI: Document tab ▸ Canvas ▸ Blending.",
                ]),
        ]
        // The file rows — Media, Captions, Rendering and export — are
        // `AgentCatalog+Files.swift`'s (captions built in `+Captions`,
        // rendering and export in `+Render`, `record_screen` in
        // `+Recording`). They are the catalog's LAST three
        // groups, so this splice is an append and the order is unchanged;
        // `ticks` is the one local they share with the groups above.
        // The dev tools' rows (AgentServer+DevTools.swift) go HERE, before the file
        // tools, never at the end; Distribution's are none.
        catalog += devTools()
        catalog += fileTools(ticks: ticks)
        let data = try JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: catalog)
        return String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)
    }
}

# The capture spike — road map 11, V1 (2026-09-26)

Four questions V2's `snapshot_ui` and `perform_menu_item` cannot be designed
without, and the instrument that measures them. **The answers are not here**:
they are in `archive/roadmap-11.md`'s V1 record (condensed in
`designs/adr/roadmap-11-dev-tools.md`), which also lists
what they changed in V2's text. What is here is how to run it again.

- **q1** — the preview well of a live, on-screen editor under `cacheDisplay`,
  and which way of putting a still under the canvas overlay for a capture
  keeps the overlay on top and leaves the view tree as it was;
- **q2** — a sheet put up by a menu item with the main run loop still free,
  captured and closed; and the inventory of which menu items reach a sheet, a
  window, or a modal run loop;
- **q3** — switching a live window's appearance, capturing and restoring;
- **q4** — `hasAmbiguousLayout` and "intrinsic width > frame width" in an
  `-O`, whole-module build.

```sh
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py                  # all four, over the bundle route
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py --only q2,q4     # a subset; other rows carry forward
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py --rebuild        # rebuild the probe regardless
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py --route direct   # the bare binary; takes no focus
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py --bundle-only    # build, assemble, check; launches nothing
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py --activation     # the activation mode over both routes
```

**How it launches (issue batch B70, #132).** Every run assembles
`work/capture_spike/CaptureProbe.app` after the build: the binary as
`Contents/MacOS/capture_probe`; `Fonts/`, `Blank.mp4`, `default.metallib`,
`GraphicTemplates/` and `GraphicsAPI.md` in `Contents/Resources/`; an
`Info.plist` (`com.kgalligan.framejob.captureprobe`, `NSPrincipalClass
NSApplication`, `LSMinimumSystemVersion 26.0`); signed ad hoc with
`codesign --force --sign -`. A failed assembly or signing fails B0 as
`bundle: <why>`. The default route, `--route bundle`, launches each mode
through LaunchServices — `open -n -W -F --stdout <png>/<mode>.out --stderr
<png>/<mode>.err CaptureProbe.app --args <mode> <fixtures> <png>` — so the
probe is a real app that can be made the active one, and reads the `ANSWER`
line from the `.out` file. `--route direct` runs the bare binary as every
run before B70 did; on this host it never becomes active, so its S and A
rows skip with `host: probe not active`. The probe finds its fonts through
`ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory` (a bare binary's `resourceURL` is its
own folder, so the direct route reads the same `Fonts/`), and its
`ProbeAppDelegate` answers LaunchServices' open-untitled and reopen events
with no. `--bundle-only` checks the bundle without launching it:
`plutil -lint`, `codesign --verify --strict`, the executable the built
binary (compared with both signatures removed, since `codesign` rewrites the
linker's), every resource present. `--activation` runs the probe's
`activation` mode (`ProbeSupport.runActivation`: `well.framejob` opened,
`activate`, and the count of visible windows) over `direct`, the CONTROL,
then `bundle`, 60 s each, and prints `activation <route>: active <bool> in
<ms|None> ms, key <bool>, visible windows <n>`; exit 0 when the bundle route
was active and key with exactly 1 visible window, 1 when not, 2 when a route
gave no answer. Neither `--bundle-only` nor `--activation` reads or writes
`answers.json`, and `activation` is not one of `rows.py`'s modes, so a full
run is still 38 rows with the same digest scheme.

**A bundle-route run takes keyboard focus** and puts the probe's windows in
front for the length of the run (about 3 minutes in full; `--activation`
about a minute and a half), so run it only when nobody is typing at the Mac.

# The capture spike — road map 11, V1 (2026-09-26)

Four questions V2's `snapshot_ui` and `perform_menu_item` cannot be designed
without, and the instrument that measures them. **The answers are not here**:
they are in `archive/roadmap-11.md`'s V1 record (condensed in
`designs/adr/roadmap-11-dev-tools.md`), which also lists
what they changed in V2's text. What is here is how to run it again.

- **q1** — the preview well of a live, on-screen editor under `cacheDisplay`,
  and which way of putting a still under the canvas overlay for a capture
  keeps the overlay on top and leaves the view tree as it was;
- **q2** — a sheet put up by a menu item with the main run loop still free,
  captured and closed; and the inventory of which menu items reach a sheet, a
  window, or a modal run loop;
- **q3** — switching a live window's appearance, capturing and restoring;
- **q4** — `hasAmbiguousLayout` and "intrinsic width > frame width" in an
  `-O`, whole-module build.

```sh
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py                  # all four, over the bundle route
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py --only q2,q4     # a subset; other rows carry forward
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py --rebuild        # rebuild the probe regardless
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py --route direct   # the bare binary; takes no focus
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py --bundle-only    # build, assemble, check; launches nothing
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/capture_spike.py --activation     # the activation mode over both routes
```

**How it launches (issue batch B70, #132).** Every run assembles
`work/capture_spike/CaptureProbe.app` after the build: the binary as
`Contents/MacOS/capture_probe`; `Fonts/`, `Blank.mp4`, `default.metallib`,
`GraphicTemplates/` and `GraphicsAPI.md` in `Contents/Resources/`; an
`Info.plist` (`com.kgalligan.framejob.captureprobe`, `NSPrincipalClass
NSApplication`, `LSMinimumSystemVersion 26.0`); signed ad hoc with
`codesign --force --sign -`. A failed assembly or signing fails B0 as
`bundle: <why>`. The default route, `--route bundle`, launches each mode
through LaunchServices — `open -n -W -F --stdout <png>/<mode>.out --stderr
<png>/<mode>.err CaptureProbe.app --args <mode> <fixtures> <png>` — so the
probe is a real app that can be made the active one, and reads the `ANSWER`
line from the `.out` file. `--route direct` runs the bare binary as every
run before B70 did; on this host it never becomes active, so its S and A
rows skip with `host: probe not active`. The probe finds its fonts through
`ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory` (a bare binary's `resourceURL` is its
own folder, so the direct route reads the same `Fonts/`), and its
`ProbeAppDelegate` answers LaunchServices' open-untitled and reopen events
with no. `--bundle-only` checks the bundle without launching it:
`plutil -lint`, `codesign --verify --strict`, the executable the built
binary (compared with both signatures removed, since `codesign` rewrites the
linker's), every resource present. `--activation` runs the probe's
`activation` mode (`ProbeSupport.runActivation`: `well.framejob` opened,
`activate`, and the count of visible windows) over `direct`, the CONTROL,
then `bundle`, 60 s each, and prints `activation <route>: active <bool> in
<ms|None> ms, key <bool>, visible windows <n>`; exit 0 when the bundle route
was active and key with exactly 1 visible window, 1 when not, 2 when a route
gave no answer. Neither `--bundle-only` nor `--activation` reads or writes
`answers.json`, and `activation` is not one of `rows.py`'s modes, so a full
run is still 38 rows with the same digest scheme.

**A bundle-route run takes keyboard focus** and puts the probe's windows in
front for the length of the run (about 3 minutes in full; `--activation`
about a minute and a half), so run it only when nobody is typing at the Mac.

# Frame Job — design and implementation spec

**The normative spec, one file per section.** It was one 4,780-line file,
`designs/reelcut-design.md`, until 2026-09-26 (git history has it). Section numbers are
unchanged, so a citation like "spec §7.3" is `07.3-frame-recipe.md` and "spec §11 W-8" is found
through [`11-decisions/README.md`](11-decisions/README.md).

**Never read the whole spec.** Read this index, then only the file for the section you need.
For a decision, look its ID up in `11-decisions/README.md`, or grep this directory
(`grep -rn "W-8 —" designs/spec/`). A file that grows past ~500 lines splits by subsection into
lettered files that keep its number (§4.3 is `04.3a`, `04.3b` and `04.3c`, §5.2 is `05.2a` and `05.2b`, §6 is `06a`, `06b` and `06c`, §7.5 is `07.5a` and `07.5b`, §7.9 is `07.9a`, `07.9b`, `07.9c` and `07.9d`);
a citation of the bare number names them together, and this index gets their rows in the same
change. Until #342 (2026-10-24) §4.3b was the Media, Document and Assistant tabs, now §4.3c; an older citation of §4.3b (in `archive/` or git history) means §4.3c.

The Lines column is `wc -l`; the `11-decisions/` cell is that folder's total, its README
included, and `make test` checks both (`tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py`).

| File | Lines | Read it for |
|---|---|---|
| [`01-what-this-is.md`](01-what-this-is.md) | 46 | The product in one page, its opening flow, and its non-goals. |
| [`02-six-ideas.md`](02-six-ideas.md) | 26 | The six ideas the model is built on, and why it stays simple. |
| [`03-window-layout.md`](03-window-layout.md) | 62 | The window's regions, as the design handoff specifies them. |
| **§4 — The regions in detail** | | |
| [`04.1-toolbar.md`](04.1-toolbar.md) | 25 | The toolbar. |
| [`04.2-preview-canvas.md`](04.2-preview-canvas.md) | 171 | The preview canvas: selection, handles, crop and region modes, on-canvas text, snapping, Show Ungraded and the scopes panel (its two slots, their sizes and the four scopes drawn). |
| [`04.3a-inspector-clip-tab.md`](04.3a-inspector-clip-tab.md) | 141 | The inspector's tab strip and its Clip tab: the sub-tabs and pinned block, the selection header and name field, sections, row marks, Reset/Clear, the note on the section list, and the controls the sections use (Rasterize's `OptionControls`). |
| [`04.3b-inspector-clip-sections.md`](04.3b-inspector-clip-sections.md) | 388 | The Clip tab's sections: every video, audio, text and shape section. |
| [`04.3c-inspector-media-document-assistant.md`](04.3c-inspector-media-document-assistant.md) | 228 | The inspector's Media tab (find band, rows, drags, Consolidate, import), the File menu's caption commands (Import, Generate and Export Captions), the Document tab and the Assistant tab. |
| [`04.4-timeline.md`](04.4-timeline.md) | 217 | The timeline: its bar, the level meter, ruler, tracks, clip bodies, gestures, entering a nest. |
| **§5 — Editing model** | | |
| [`05.1-time.md`](05.1-time.md) | 23 | Ticks (600 000 per second), frame rates, snapping to the grid. |
| [`05.2a-project-schema-canvas-media-video.md`](05.2a-project-schema-canvas-media-video.md) | 369 | The project JSON schema (format version 27): what a patch means, the example document, `source`, `canvas`, `media[]`, `graphic`, an action end's graphic and speed, `enabled`, and every `video.*` field. |
| [`05.2b-project-schema-audio-text-shape-tracks.md`](05.2b-project-schema-audio-text-shape-tracks.md) | 187 | The schema's `audio.*`, `text.*` and `shape.*` fields, `actions[].end` and `transition_in`, a clip's `name` and `label`, `tracks[].solo` and `matte`, `nests`, ids, and what is not in the model. |
| [`05.3-placement.md`](05.3-placement.md) | 81 | Where a layer lands on the canvas: position, scale, crop, regions, reflection, motion, nests flattened. |
| [`05.4-actions.md`](05.4-actions.md) | 156 | Actions (keyframed segments): what they target, how lists interpolate, a stored `null` as off. |
| [`05.5-purity-and-undo.md`](05.5-purity-and-undo.md) | 40 | An edit's three answers, purity, undo. |
| [`05.6-persistence.md`](05.6-persistence.md) | 228 | The package on disk: Consolidate, bookmarks, reversed assets, ramp audio, caches and their markers, transcripts. |
| **§6 — Edit operations: exact semantics** | | |
| [`06a-edit-operations-shared-rules.md`](06a-edit-operations-shared-rules.md) | 84 | The rules every op shares: caller ticks snapped to the frame grid, an omitted argument against `null`, how to read a "refuses", the one way a patch is read, and the `scope` envelope key (the view project, the eight ops that are an error with a scope, the checks on the merged parent). |
| [`06b-edit-operations-clips.md`](06b-edit-operations-clips.md) | 443 | Every clip op: add, insert and overwrite, the two backgrounds; move and the overlap rule; the trims, roll, slip, rate stretch, speed and reverse; split, the ripple deletes and range cuts; freeze, detach, duplicate, paste and paste attributes; nest and unnest; the patch ops; the transition ops. |
| [`06c-edit-operations-actions-tracks-media.md`](06c-edit-operations-actions-tracks-media.md) | 209 | The action ops (the zoom action, end patches and `off`); the track, marker, canvas and media ops; and the op table's two halves (the arguments half is `core/src/op_table.rs`). |
| **§7 — Architecture: Rust decides, AVFoundation and Metal do** | | |
| [`07-architecture.md`](07-architecture.md) | 25 | The Rust/platform split in one page. |
| [`07.1-ffi-surface.md`](07.1-ffi-surface.md) | 192 | The `rc_*` exports and their contracts. |
| [`07.2-composition-plan.md`](07.2-composition-plan.md) | 202 | The composition plan: A/B assignment, speed and freeze, audio envelopes, instructions. |
| [`07.3-frame-recipe.md`](07.3-frame-recipe.md) | 488 | The per-frame recipe the compositor draws: layers, mattes, nests, recipe options, burn-in, ungraded. |
| [`07.4-swift-file-map.md`](07.4-swift-file-map.md) | 60 | The spec's Swift file map (app/CLAUDE.md is the live one). |
| [`07.5a-compositor-step-0-output.md`](07.5a-compositor-step-0-output.md) | 204 | The Metal compositor's pixel formats, step 0 (per composition) and camera log, the request and the scopes' tap (the shown set, the kernels, the counting rule), the HLG working space, the output pass and linear light. |
| [`07.5b-compositor-passes-grades.md`](07.5b-compositor-passes-grades.md) | 326 | The compositor's per-layer passes and pipelines, the adjustment pass and its qualifier, the encoded-sRGB blend, transitions, mattes, tone, wheels, curves, looks and `.cube` LUTs, and the frame budget. |
| [`07.6-playback-update-rules.md`](07.6-playback-update-rules.md) | 46 | What playback does after every edit: rebuild or refresh. |
| [`07.7-import.md`](07.7-import.md) | 240 | `MediaImporter.probe`, the formats import accepts, the WebM/Matroska rewrap and its PQ copy's HDR10 fields, its copy's progress window, the copy's original, and the opt-in ffmpeg step's original and checked VP9 copy. |
| [`07.8-export.md`](07.8-export.md) | 651 | Export: writers, formats, loudness, the queue, the wait for ramp audio. |
| [`07.9a-agent-tools.md`](07.9a-agent-tools.md) | 484 | The MCP agent's tools: one tool per op plus `scope`, the parity check and the argument gate, the app-state tools, lenient decoding. |
| [`07.9b-agent-lane-assistant.md`](07.9b-agent-lane-assistant.md) | 160 | The agent lane every tool call goes through, the bundled helper, the assistant session (its key, prices and spend), its prompt, and the Assistant tab as the session's door. |
| [`07.9c-agent-graphics-dev-tools-transport.md`](07.9c-agent-graphics-dev-tools-transport.md) | 312 | The graphics loop's tools (write, read, render, import, delete, rename and restore a module), an action's graphic props and the graphics menus, the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`, `perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `assistant_send` / `assistant_answer` and their launch defaults, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`), and the transport (the Unix socket, `framejob-mcp`, Copy MCP Command). |
| [`07.9d-agent-recording.md`](07.9d-agent-recording.md) | 46 | `record_screen`, File ▸ New Recording…'s mirror: its arguments, the grants it reads and never asks, its refusal order, a paused recording's segments, the voice-over, a camera alone and a camera beside the screen, and its answer. |
| [`07.10-rust-module-map.md`](07.10-rust-module-map.md) | 110 | The spec's Rust module map (core/CLAUDE.md is the live one). |
| [`08-repo-layout.md`](08-repo-layout.md) | 66 | Repo layout, build, conventions. |
| [`09-keys-and-menus.md`](09-keys-and-menus.md) | 197 | The keyboard map and every menu, and keys proposed but not yet bound. |
| [`10-milestones.md`](10-milestones.md) | 70 | M1–M3 in build order; each step's *Verify* is an acceptance test. |
| [`11-decisions/`](11-decisions/README.md) | 14542 in 33 files | Every decision already made, indexed by ID. |

## The original preface

**Status: accepted and built** (M1–M3, then road maps 2–12; `designs/adr/` has each one's
record). The preface below is the original handoff's, kept for its reading order.

Sibling of `~/devel/rasterize` — the same shape (Swift/AppKit app over a Rust staticlib core, a
hand-maintained C header as the one contract, xcodegen, an embedded MCP agent), a different domain.
Where this document says "as in Rasterize" it names the file to copy from.

Reading order for an implementer: §1–2 (the product), §5–7 (model, ops,
architecture — the parts with exact schemas), §10 (build order), then §3–4
when building the UI, §8–9 for conventions and keys, §11 for the decisions
already made so they are not re-litigated.

that nothing persists — none writes a default; Show Selection is disabled
while off with no adjustment clip selected, Show SDR Version is always
enabled and shows an HLG project's SDR version with an "SDR Version" tag)),
Window (Minimize,
Zoom, Export Queue — road map 2's phase 7e, the export sheet's Add to Queue
button's other end, with no key equivalent because §9's "proposed, not yet
bound" table claims no row for it and every bare letter belongs to the
editor's own `keyDown`; the queue's window sets
`isExcludedFromWindowsMenu`, since this menu is `NSApp.windowsMenu` and
AppKit would otherwise list it a second time under its own title — Bring All
to Front), Help (Frame Job Help, Graphics Reference — road map 10's G5b: the
bundled `GraphicsAPI.md` opened in the person's own app, live while the
bundle holds it, with no document needed).
Road map 10's G5b adds **Insert**, right after Edit, holding **Graphic ▸**:
one item per bundled template (the twenty-three of `graphic/tests/graphics/`, copied
into the app's `GraphicTemplates/`, titled from the file stem —
`lower-third.js` is Lower Third — never by compiling it), a separator and
From File…; and File gains **Add Font to Graphics…** and **Add Image to
Graphics…** right after Consolidate Media…. None of the twenty-seven items takes a
key equivalent, for the caption items' reason; §11 G-16 has the rules.
Issue batch B84 (#103) adds, after a separator straight under Add Image to
Graphics… and before the separator above Export…, **Rename Graphic…**,
**Delete Graphic…** and **Restore Graphic Version…**, in that order and
with no key equivalents: each is one small sheet over the body its tool
runs (`rename_graphic`, `delete_graphic`, `restore_graphic`). Rename and
Delete are greyed in a project with no graphics, Restore when no version
of any graphic is kept, and Rename also while a nest is open; §11 G-30 has
the rules.
Grading GR4b puts **Adjustment Clip** first in Insert, above
Graphic ▸, with no key equivalent: one adjustment clip over the In/Out range,
else the selected clips' span, else the whole timeline, on the front track

  `ReelCore.swift`.** A change like adding `scope` edits the struct and its factories together.
  `coreNames()` calls `rc_*`, and only `ReelCore.swift` may do that. `OpArgs` stayed `private`
  because it moved along with every user it has (orig file map, `ReelCore` · `ReelOps`).
- **Any addition to `ReelCore.swift` pays for itself first with a pure move of a type that names
  no `rc_*` symbol.** The precedents are `RecipeSource.swift`, `TextPatch.swift` and
  `MediaDescriptor.swift`. The file is far over the cap (orig "ReelCore.swift toll", "graphics
  wrappers").

  wrapper (#111, spec §11 SR-20) landed: `ReelTime.perSecond`, `ticks(seconds:)` and
  `seconds(_:)` went whole to an `extension ReelTime` in `CoreValues.swift`, and the
  JSON-reading half of `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` to `ReelOpSchema.table(from:)`, the
  `rc_op_schemas()` call staying; a pure move gated alone, nothing widened. `wc -l
  app/Sources/ReelCore.swift`: 803 before, 774 after; `CoreValues.swift` is 116. The next seam is
  still `jsonArray`.
  Codec-export C1 paid it (toll T2) before `ReelAV1` (`rc_av1_*`, spec §11 CX-12 (4)) landed:
  `jsonArray` went whole to `CoreJSON.array` in `CoreValues.swift` (internal where it was
  `private`; its two callers, `snapCandidates(excluding:)` and `ReelSnap.resolve`, renamed),
  a pure move gated alone by `make typecheck`. `wc -l app/Sources/ReelCore.swift`: 789 before, 782
  after; `CoreValues.swift` 138 → 147. `ReelAV1` then took ReelCore to 859, over the cap.
  C1's fix pass paid that back before merge in two pure moves, each gated alone by `make
  typecheck` (exit 0, the four baseline warnings): first `ReelAV1.Config` (with its hex decoder)
  and `ReelAV1.Color` went whole to an `extension ReelAV1` in `CoreValues.swift` (859 → 823;
  `CoreValues.swift` 147 → 187); then the `rc_*`-free halves of five members went there too —

  header's payment list (lines 13–37) became one sentence pointing at this entry, and `scoped`'s

  every type left names an `rc_*` symbol.

  spec §11 CX-17), taking the file to 804, and its fix pass paid it back, a pure move gated

# added here in the same commit as the tool because this set is asserted
# EXACTLY below and a new scopeless tool would otherwise fail phase 9's own
# catalog row for the right reason at the wrong address.
APP_STATE_TOOLS = {
    "open_project", "new_project", "save_project", "get_project", "import_media",
    "import_captions", "export_captions", "transcribe", "consolidate_media",
    "detect_silence", "normalize_clip", "set_playhead", "set_range", "set_selection",
    "set_scope", "undo", "redo", "render_frame", "export", "record_screen",
    "write_graphic", "get_graphic", "graphic_reference", "render_graphic",
